S.name: Break a specific "fixed" assumption, not the generic one
S.detail: Accepted members name what was previously static — a human-designed strategy repertoire, predefined task categories, a fixed memory schema, a monolithic summary, manually authored skills — and make that thing learnable; the frozen-weights framing is background, not the claim.

S.name: Contrast, not narration
S.detail: Pairing successes with failures (or repaired failures with successes) isolates what actually differed and yields guidance that complements retrieved demonstrations.

S.name: A grounding signal in the loop
S.detail: Execution feedback, verification, correctness judgments, or a self-judge whose imperfection is acknowledged decide what becomes a lesson.

S.name: Explicit maintenance once the store grows
S.detail: Localized delta edits, consolidation, forgetting thresholds, and revised retrieval hooks keep the store bounded and avoid the detail loss of rewriting it as one summary.

S.name: A gate on what is kept
S.detail: Execution tests, quality filters, or judge-controlled versioned merges decide which entries or skills survive before they are published for reuse.

F.name: Restating the parent assumption as the contribution
F.detail: 9 of 16 rejected members frame the broken assumption as "improvement without weight / parameter updates", versus 3 of 23 accepted — the move's premise offered as its novelty.

F.name: The new domain is the novelty
F.detail: Most rejected H00 members re-apply attempt → reflect → store → retrieve to one more vertical (web, database querying, navigation, customer service, attack generation, clinical deliberation, simulated markets, productivity tasks) with a generic signature.

F.name: Casting the store as a stand-in optimizer
F.detail: Group-relative "semantic advantages", graded state-space search over edits, or library updates presented as replacing weight-based optimization set up a head-to-head with the optimizer they claim to replace.

F.name: A retrieval fix presented as learning
F.detail: Evolving entries' applicability conditions to correct retrieval misalignment is mechanism-wise a retrieval improvement and must be argued as one.

F.name: No outcome-grounded store at all
F.detail: Prompting for metacognition or self-assessment, or abstracting schemas from a demonstration or factoring a prompt into shared and residual parts, reuses structure rather than experience.

S.name: Reward the improvement, not the score
S.detail: Accepted proposers reward the change relative to the pre-edit state, the previous episode, or a dominance relation, which separates edit quality from query difficulty.

S.name: Credit through downstream use
S.detail: Accepted curators are rewarded by what a consumer does with the written artifact (answer correctness after retrieval, reader traversal), not by the episode that produced it.

S.name: Co-train or couple writer and reader
S.detail: Keeping the improver aligned with the policy that consumes its output stops stored skills and designs from going stale as the rollout distribution shifts.

S.name: Train a new kind of object
S.detail: Accepted H27 members produce a query-conditioned distribution over designs, a single-pass system program, or a self-rectifying generator team — not a familiar generator with a new loss.

S.name: Meta-train across task families
S.detail: Accepted members that compress examples into instructions or generate systems train across many diverse datasets, so the improver learns reusable composition rather than one task.

F.name: Optimizer swap on a known loop
F.detail: 3 of the 4 high-fit rejected workflow/system generators keep the "generate, execute, score, train the generator" recipe and change only the training procedure.

F.name: Pattern at the edge
F.detail: 7 of 11 rejected H27 members are low-fit (the trained policy is a generic controller, data acquirer, or code optimizer) versus 2 of 10 accepted; the amortization story then does not carry the paper.

F.name: One bolted-on property
F.detail: Rejected generators add paraphrase invariance or safety feedback to an existing generator loop, so the property, not the trained improver, is the stated contribution.

F.name: Composite proxy reward on an isolated writer
F.detail: The one rejected H26 member trains the writer alone on task accuracy mixed with validity, format, and compression terms, rather than coupling it to the reader.

S.name: Attribution scope matches the artifact's structure
S.detail: The minimal execution subgraph, section or module that produced the failure is edited, not the whole artifact; deep global chains grow and lose specificity.

S.name: Evaluation budget is steered, not spread
S.detail: Accepted mechanisms decide where scoring goes (bandit selection over a beam, tree search over future rewrites, local refinement before bounded nudges to neighbors).

S.name: The retention rule protects earlier wins
S.detail: Successes are fed alongside failures, edits are accepted only if they individually improve, illegal or regressing updates are rolled back.

S.name: Mechanisms are diagnosed, not instances
S.detail: Traces are clustered across tasks before an edit is proposed, so one repair serves a failure family instead of one trajectory.

S.name: The proposer sees raw evidence
S.detail: Full traces, source and the candidate history beat fixed summaries for localizing faults that text-only rewriting cannot reach (routing, state, tool dispatch).

S.name: The object is a general improver
S.detail: The patched artifact is the means; the method is stated for any artifact of its type, not for one task's deliverable.

F.name: The loop is the vehicle for a domain result
F.detail: Many rejected problem statements are domain tasks (table reasoning, a retrieval knowledge store, image-generation sampling, alarm analysis, game players, parallel mappers, attack generation) with the critique → rewrite loop applied unchanged.

F.name: One more signal in the update rule
F.detail: Rejected mechanisms often add an input to the textual gradient (neighbor conditioning, response-history similarity, contrast of best and worst prompts, sample-state cues) while topology, selection and certification stay as before.

F.name: A single executable program is evolved
F.detail: Mapper, RL-agent and game-player generators improve one deliverable against its own benchmark; that reads as program synthesis, not harness improvement.

F.name: Self-constructed validation replaces ground truth
F.detail: Several rejected loops build their own validation (probe-derived tool cases, synthetic examples, pseudo-labels, label-free inference-time feedback), so the signal that certifies the edit comes from the same model family that proposes it.

F.name: Feedback is assumed to isolate the edited artifact
F.detail: Editing a knowledge store from expert feedback, or a prompt from a critique, presumes the failure was caused there; nothing in the mechanism checks it.

F.name: Guards are mistaken for a contribution
F.detail: Section-level edits and preservation tests appear in rejected mechanisms too; they are necessary hygiene, not a differentiator.

S.name: A named retention test decides which criteria survive
S.detail: Reward variance across samples, correlation with a verifiable outcome or a strict validation gate keeps the rubric from collapsing into a constant or a target.

S.name: The anchor is isolated from the candidates
S.detail: A separate surrogate verifier checked against opaque oracle bits, or expectations formed before the candidate is seen, removes the grader's drift toward agreeing.

S.name: Criteria are grounded in evidence the policy did not produce
S.detail: Retrieved evidence and paired positive/negative criteria are load-bearing in the high-fit accepted rubric-reward member.

S.name: New evaluation items earn their place through reproducible checks
S.detail: Recorded trajectories or deterministic probes let a benchmark get harder while staying solvable.

S.name: The evolved component is ablated and its cost is stated
S.detail: Of the 6 corpus members with evidence blocks, 2 report a retained-artifact ablation; one reports 27000 H100 GPU hours beyond supervised fine-tuning.

S.name: The evaluator need not be prose
S.detail: Adaptive objective weights and online reward/bonus filtering were accepted as low-fit instances of the same move.

F.name: Closed self-contained loop
F.detail: The mechanism co-trains task generator, solver and reward model on one shared backbone, so nothing outside the loop checks the supervision it produces.

F.name: One-shot calibration on a small human batch
F.detail: The mechanism fits the evaluator once to a few human ratings and then optimizes against it, so its fidelity is bounded by that batch.

F.name: Selection and validation on the same labels
F.detail: Choosing criteria or demonstrations by correlation with the labeled set that also scores them is not an independent validity test.

F.name: Dynamic evaluation without a certificate
F.detail: Competition, prompt optimization or adaptive test hardening changes what is measured, but no anchor certifies that the new measurement is valid.

S.name: One rollout stream serves both levers
S.detail: When the same on-policy rollouts rank context candidates and drive the weight update, the coupling interface is the data itself and cannot be dismissed as two optimizers in sequence.

S.name: Each lever has a distinct, typed job
S.detail: Declarative knowledge refined in context, procedural competence trained into weights; the split makes a lever-wise ablation meaningful.

S.name: The policy is trained to condition on the context artifact
S.detail: A skill or memory library that is an explicit input of the trained policy, and is revised from diagnosed failures as well as successes, keeps both sides aligned.

S.name: Internalization shrinks the context
S.detail: Compressing trajectory-heavy experience into a few learnable tokens or adapters on a frozen backbone, with recent insights kept as text, answers the "memory grows without bound" plateau.

S.name: Memory pays for itself
S.detail: Retrieved test-time memories that are curated into training data turn an inference cost into a training asset.

F.name: Weight-side machinery carries the paper
F.detail: 4 of 6 rejected mechanisms center on a new weight-update procedure (bi-level meta-RL, capacity expansion with synthetic rehearsal, selective single-step RL, per-module policy gradients); the context lever is secondary, so "coupling" reads as composition.

F.name: Context as a recall store, not a trained-on input
F.detail: Where the context side is a bank that retains and recalls prior solutions or knowledge, the policy is not shown to be trained to read it, so neither lever depends on the other.

F.name: Sequenced, not coupled
F.detail: Composing an existing policy-gradient recipe with a prompt optimizer, or integrating retrieved principles "with RL", leaves no shared interface (shared rollouts, versioned data, conditioning).

F.name: Confidence-selected consolidation
F.detail: A design that consolidates high-confidence traces into a learned component risks baking confident-but-wrong behavior into weights unless curation is anchored in verifiable outcomes.

F.name: Test-time evolution with no declared split
F.detail: A loop that accumulates experience on its incoming query stream makes the adaptation stream and the reported stream coincide unless a split is fixed in advance.

S.name: The admission gate is execution, not judgment
S.detail: Replayed task success, evidence the skill was actually invoked, and an observable state change keep the action space from filling with plausible but broken code.

S.name: Each admitted artifact is a capability increment
S.detail: Admitting only what the current policy cannot cheaply re-derive, or only patterns that have recurred, keeps the library compact and every entry load-bearing.

S.name: The abstraction is validated, not just the original instance
S.detail: A tool that solves the problem it came from is a cached trajectory until it is checked on inputs it was not built from.

S.name: Repair is driven by obtainable signals
S.detail: Tracebacks, reproducible environment snapshots and trace-level responsibility let a first draft converge, and keep edits local instead of rewriting the library.

S.name: The retained library is shown to carry the gain
S.detail: A retained-artifact ablation is the most common strength among the 19 corpus members with a quote-grounded evidence block (yes in 10).

S.name: Generation is grounded where model knowledge runs out
S.detail: External code, documentation or demonstrations anchor tools the backbone could not write from memory.

F.name: The artifact is buried inside a larger architecture
F.detail: In four of H07's seven rejected members, forging sits inside a hierarchical memory, a multi-agent scheme, a workflow planner or a trained arbitration policy, so no isolated test of the executable artifact exists.

F.name: The "skill" stops being verifiable code
F.detail: Recasting skills as trained control policies with generated rewards or evolved symbolic interpretations forfeits the execution check that gives the move its advantage.

F.name: The skill source is a human, not the agent
F.detail: Encoding human corrections into stored skills makes the library grow through supervision, which weakens the self-improvement claim.

F.name: Reuse is bounded by a fixed input shape
F.detail: Templates generated offline from a schema are reusable only on inputs sharing that schema — caching, not open-ended capability growth.

F.name: Structure is validated by review, not execution
F.detail: Consolidating tools by semantic similarity and letting an agent judge that function was preserved leaves equivalence unverified (one H08 member; tentative).

S.name: One alternative explanation, one targeted cut
S.detail: Accepted diagnostics name the cheaper story (search budget, prompt length, feedback reuse) and pick the single intervention that falsifies it.

S.name: The retained artifact is ablated directly
S.detail: In the evidence audit (corpus papers only), 4 of the 5 accepted controlled-intervention members report a retained-artifact ablation. It is the move's signature.

S.name: Evaluation is held apart from the loop
S.detail: Held-out or separated tasks, a frozen scorer, and leakage that is *tested* rather than assumed. Of the 6 audited corpus papers with a tested leakage guard, 3 sit here.

S.name: Negative and conditional results are the headline
S.detail: Noisy memory hurting, poor transfer of evolved artifacts, fabricated guardrails: accepted work reports these as findings.

S.name: A mitigation or acceptance rule is paired with the diagnosis
S.detail: Gated consolidation, warrant-aware edit acceptance, or a defense, even one that only partly restores performance or safety.

S.name: The isolating control *is* the mechanism
S.detail: Frozen-generation feedback injection, compute-matched held-out comparison, a planted nonexistent failure, a protected protocol: the cut carries the paper, not a side ablation.

F.name: An end-to-end sweep passed off as a diagnosis
F.detail: Comparing model pairings or methods without a matched control leaves the gain confounded with budget.

F.name: A normative benchmark with no frozen view
F.detail: Arguing that agents *should* be tested on lifelong learning, then headlining that current models fail, reads as descriptive rather than diagnostic.

F.name: A benchmark bundled with a new method
F.detail: The contribution splits and neither half is evaluated cleanly.

F.name: Single-interaction attacks with no persistence trace
F.detail: Showing one injected record redirects later answers, without tracing it across sessions or generations, leaves the "persistent" claim unexamined.

F.name: A defense offered in place of a diagnosis
F.detail: Consensus self-validation over memory-derived reasoning paths is proposed as the fix before the poisoning dynamics it targets are isolated.

F.name: Relative standing scored instead of artifact effect
F.detail: Iterated open-ended tournaments rank agents but do not show that the strategy code they produce improves learning.

S.name: An explicit counterfactual behind every credit
S.detail: Accepted members contrast memory-on with memory-off runs, or use the generator's own reliance on an entry; utility without a baseline is only correlation with success.

S.name: Admission paired with retirement
S.detail: The accepted library member combines a prior on how entries are authored with conservative retirement and a hard size bound; either gate alone lets the collection degrade silently.

S.name: A named silent failure that governance demonstrably fixes
S.detail: Showing that ungoverned accumulation degrades retrieval and injects harmful guidance makes the gate a remedy rather than overhead.

S.name: The gate's effect is ablatable by design
S.detail: Accepted mechanisms keep the value signal or the gate as a separable component (a reranker, a reweighting rule, a stopping rule), so stripping it is a clean ablation.

S.name: Cost of the gate stated openly
S.detail: Accepted members list the extra contrastive run, online-learning expense, or a large call overhead against a no-skill baseline instead of hiding it.

S.name: Theory that separates error types
S.detail: The accepted formal members distinguish compounding optimization errors from non-compounding knowledge errors, and drift from apparent quality gains, and stop on constraints first.

F.name: Infrastructure offered as the gate
F.detail: A rejected member versions and registers every refined component under one protocol and lets execution feedback refine them, but its mechanism contains no measured admission or retirement test; versioning enables rollback without deciding what is kept.

F.name: Utility routed into training of something else
F.detail: Rejected memory members push entry value into policy gradients, embedding updates or prior refinement, so the memory's own effect is never isolated.

F.name: A self-reinforcing loop with no fixed referee
F.detail: One rejected design lets memory values refine the model prior, whose better trajectories then enrich the memory; the loop has no step that can reject an entry.

F.name: Credit that needs paired rollouts to exist
F.detail: The guided-versus-unguided reward difference is a sound counterfactual, but it doubles execution and, by that design's own stated limit, retrieving many strategies adds noise.

F.name: Gating the retriever rather than the content
F.detail: Online embedding updates from task success change what is found without ever deciding what is kept, so nothing harmful is demoted or removed.

S.name: The case unit is re-bindable
S.detail: Stripping instance-specific values or cutting episodes into functional subtasks is what lets precedents compose instead of merely resembling the new task.

S.name: Writes are gated by an external check
S.detail: Admitting cases only after an executable test, simulation, or outcome threshold keeps unsupported patterns from accumulating as the store grows.

S.name: Content and index are decoupled
S.detail: Stable consolidated content reached through separate cues, pointers, or cluster boundaries lets one item be found by several paths without duplication.

S.name: Retrieval is selective, not maximal
S.detail: Category filters, caps on injected cases, relevance gates, and triggers at uncertain steps keep context small; injected-but-irrelevant experience is a stated harm.

S.name: The store is certified by removing it
S.detail: Among the 24 corpus members with a quote-grounded evidence audit, the retained-store ablation is the most often reported item (12 of 24).

S.name: Updates are local and cheap
S.detail: Accepted structure-centric designs touch only affected clusters or subtrees, use separate update rates for fast facts and slow traits, and defer heavy consolidation off the online path.

F.name: The store is incidental to the method
F.detail: Several rejected designs are exemplar selection, synthetic demonstrations, context-chunk covering, or simulation-scored best-of-N — not a growing, reused store; 7 of 16 rejected members are low-fit to the move.

F.name: Similar-looking is taken as applicable
F.detail: Retrieval that trades task-distribution distance against utility matches on resemblance, not on whether the precedent's local reasoning transfers.

F.name: The store is built from the test stream
F.detail: A knowledge bank updated continually from test inputs makes the gain inseparable from the evaluation stream.

F.name: Model outputs enter memory without an external gate
F.detail: Stored intermediate answers or generated memories are admitted on the model's own word, so errors can propagate as the store grows.

F.name: Curation does not scale
F.detail: Manually verified examples undercut the "improves with use" claim.

F.name: A new store shape stands in for an argument
F.detail: Rejected H04 designs (sentence graphs, native key-value memory, evolving schemas, profile-plus-hierarchy) resemble accepted ones; shape alone does not separate.

S.name: A named, immutable anchor
S.detail: Accepted members state which level stays fixed (outer algorithm, promotion rule, evaluator); without it, gains cannot be attributed to the edited improver.

S.name: Improver fitness = downstream fitness of its products
S.detail: Scoring an optimizer by what it produces needs no separate quality signal and keeps the improver from grading itself on a metric it edits.

S.name: Comparison against the fixed, hand-designed improver
S.detail: It is the direct test of the claim that editing the improver helps; 6 of the 12 corpus members with an evidence audit report it (the audit covers corpus papers only).

S.name: Search cost on the table
S.detail: 6 of the 12 audited corpus members report optimizer cost; one accepted member reports about $7000 for fifteen iterations — the move is expensive and reviewers can see it.

S.name: Selection that tolerates non-improving steps
S.detail: Archiving offspring that do not beat their parent, or picking parents by subtree productivity, lets the search escape local optima that a greedy lineage cannot.

S.name: A reified, swappable learning mechanism (H21)
S.detail: Expressing memory/retrieval as one executable unit gives the strongest audited (corpus-only) profile in the parent: held-out separation and a retained-design ablation in 3 of 4 each.

F.name: Editing the task structure instead of the proposer
F.detail: The lone rejected member (low-fit) learns a reusable cross-task template and selection strategy; the edited object never generates future edits. The modes below come from limitations stated by corpus members, not from outcomes.

F.name: Self-modification breaks the loop
F.detail: Rewrites can terminate optimization; an accepted member reports fourteen percent of robustness trials ending worse than initialization. Rollback must be part of the method.

F.name: Benchmark reuse passes for self-improvement
F.detail: Repeated evaluation on small fixed subsets (held-out "no" in 2 of the 12 audited corpus members, "partial" in 2) lets the improver overfit the very score that promotes it.

F.name: Noise compounds across generations
F.detail: Variance across runs is reported by 1 of 12 audited; with few seeds, noisy evaluations falsely promote rewrites and outer-improver comparisons stay inconclusive.

F.name: The anchor leaks
F.detail: Unrestricted agents can call stronger models, LLM reviewers used as gates share blind spots, and evaluator edits require a trustworthy assessor — any of these voids the attribution.

F.name: Locally evolved mechanisms sold as general (H21)
F.detail: Transfer is shown within related regimes; in one unlabeled member most transferred designs underperform a universal seed design.

S.name: The contribution lives at the search level, not the domain
S.detail: Accepted members change what fitness measures (worst case over a shift, robustness over paraphrases, end-to-end credit across pipeline modules) or how evaluations are spent (novelty rejection, adaptive parent sampling, bandit allocation); a new metaheuristic alone rarely suffices.

S.name: The evaluator is built before the loop and is hard to game
S.detail: Execution scores, end-to-end metrics or verified correctness make selection pressure meaningful; proxies are checked for rank transfer to the real setting.

S.name: The evolved unit is small and sits in a scaffold
S.detail: Operators, priority functions or skeletons with numerically fitted constants keep children valid and the search tractable.

S.name: Mutations are grounded in what the evaluator observed
S.detail: Training curves, legality violations or failure analyses fed back to the proposer give variation a direction that selection alone does not.

S.name: Memory and archives earn their place by measured effect
S.detail: Accepted memory designs credit items by child-versus- parent fitness change and keep negative evidence; frontier designs name the axis of complementarity they preserve.

S.name: The genome is enlarged only when text-level search plateaus
S.detail: Moving from wording to whole configurations, non-text prompt parts or code is motivated by a named ceiling of the smaller genome.

F.name: A generic loop pointed at a new domain
F.detail: Most rejected members in H13 and H14 apply standard evolution to attacks, routing, solvers, kernels or feature engineering with no search-level novelty; they read as application notes.

F.name: Re-skinned metaheuristics or ensembles
F.detail: A new swarm or hierarchy metaphor, or a vote over existing optimizers, without a new objective or genome is the commonest high-fit rejected shape in H13.

F.name: Search buried inside a larger pipeline
F.detail: 14 of the 31 rejected members are low-fit, where population search is one component and its contribution cannot be isolated.

F.name: Proxy fitness in ill-specified or adversarial targets
F.detail: Several rejected designs select on a proxy (synthetic- sample precision, classifier-guided attributes) where nothing ties the proxy to the stated goal.

F.name: Orchestration in place of search
F.detail: Splitting a standard loop into cooperating agent roles, or changing a retrieval key, alters the plumbing but not the generate–evaluate–select dynamics.

F.name: Diversity as the deliverable
F.detail: Selecting a complementary set as the end product, with no executable fitness loop around it, falls outside what this move buys.

S.name: One search-shaping primitive that makes each execution count
S.detail: Accepted members win through an archive of scored stepping stones, standardized interfaces plus a cheap surrogate filter, an experience tree tying edits to measured effects, or a staged local-then-global order, not through the choice of search algorithm.

S.name: Tune components before searching wiring
S.detail: Topology search over untuned prompts measures the wrong thing; the accepted ordering is local prompt tuning, then a pruned topology search, then joint retuning.

S.name: Gate structural change on a task-outcome signal
S.detail: Pass/fail or an independent verifier decides what persists (H18 especially); the proposer's self-assessment does not.

S.name: Keep a retreat path
S.detail: A verifier allowed to prefer a simple system's answer, or escalation to deeper structure only when retained structure stalls, keeps added complexity honest.

S.name: Change the objective when search is too expensive
S.detail: Ranking compositions by tail risk or predicting a workflow's utility from its code, prompt and graph views replaces exhaustive execution.

S.name: Certify the frozen or adapted design away from where it was found
S.detail: Held-out problems at minimum; a second task family or executor model strengthens the claim.

F.name: Co-evolving every axis at once
F.detail: Roles, collaboration structure, mutation operators, curriculum and control rules evolved together with no axis-level ablation reads as a system, not a finding.

F.name: Incremental refinement of an existing search
F.detail: A tighter design representation or finer block-level blame must show that statically valid designs actually execute and that blame beats the end-to-end score.

F.name: Proxy-steered edits
F.detail: Steering roles by linguistic or embedding proxies of role clarity and complementarity, or edits by LLM-ranked failure traces, ties the search to a signal not shown to track task success (the single rejected H18 member is of this kind).

F.name: Infrastructure presented as optimization
F.detail: Modular pipeline tooling with caching and cost tracking is engineering unless it enables a search result nothing else could.

F.name: Re-parameterizing the space as the contribution
F.detail: Recasting the workflow as a trained connection matrix, or bundling dynamic reasoning construction with prompt and hyperparameter tuning, changes how designs are written down without isolating a new reason the search succeeds.

S.name: A validity anchor the generator cannot game
S.detail: Execution, generated tests, runnable repositories, retrieval checks, documents hidden from the solver, or answer-preserving variants of solved problems keep hard tasks honest.

S.name: A frontier signal tied to that anchor
S.detail: Difficulty bands, uncertainty, or learning progress measured on a fixed held-out validation environment — not on the generator's own outputs — keep the curriculum learnable.

S.name: A real per-instance or per-skill diagnostic
S.detail: Failures, high-perplexity instances, forgetting and boundary signals, or frontier accuracy decide what to make; regeneration happens every round, not once.

S.name: Verified composition and stepping stones
S.detail: Harder tasks built from verified atomic ones, or conditioned on unsolved real-data goals, inherit known solutions and stay pointed at capabilities that matter.

S.name: Cost treated as a first-class problem
S.detail: Difficulty estimation needs repeated solver rollouts; one accepted member's main contribution is making nested proposer-solver sampling affordable.

S.name: Certification outside the loop
S.detail: Held-out and cross-task gains against static-synthetic, frozen-generator, or random/heuristic curricula.

F.name: Difficulty without validity
F.detail: In H22, 4 of 5 rejected members reward progress, difficulty, diversity or learnability with no stated independent validity check.

F.name: A schedule dressed as a diagnosis
F.detail: In H23, 3 of 8 rejected members raise difficulty by a generic schedule (deeper composition, difficulty buckets, a solved-level floor) rather than by a measured weakness.

F.name: A learned proxy as the only certificate
F.detail: 2 of 8 rejected H23 members certify with a reward model or a model-judged success signal, so the curriculum inherits the proxy's errors.

F.name: The learner as its own improvement source
F.detail: A rejected loop feeds a small student's action divergences back into synthesis, so what gets generated is bounded by what that student can reveal about itself.
